- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often overshoots early in forecast horizon; cap peak forecasts at 1–2% above recent high.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline in forecast, reduce subsequent values by 0.5–1.5% to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp drop (e.g., 2–3 days) after a peak, model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% on days 3–7 post-peak.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.67), model overfits to recent momentum; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to the first 5–7 days of forecast.
